message.content:
Search this repository very thoroughly for:

1. Webhook or outbound HTTP notification delivery - where the server actually sends HTTP requests to external systems when content changes. Look for functions that execute/deliver/send webhooks or notifications over HTTP. Search for terms like "webhook", "deliver", "notify", "outbound", "httpClient", "fetch", "request" in the context of sending notifications.

2. SSRF protection - any mechanism that validates/filters URLs to prevent requests to internal network addresses (localhost, 127.0.0.1, 10.x, 192.168.x, private IPs, etc.). Search for terms like "ssrf", "private", "internal", "blocked", "localhost", "127.0.0.1", "isPrivate", "validateUrl", "allowedHost".

Report the exact file paths, function names, and line numbers for both. Be very thorough - check multiple directories and naming conventions.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

86	// TestPostSignsRequest verifies the end-to-end Standard Webhooks signature so a
87	// receiver following the documented verification recipe will accept our requests.
88	func TestPostSignsRequest(t *testing.T) {
89		// httptest listens on 127.0.0.1, which the SSRF guard blocks by default.
90		prev := AllowPrivateIPs
91		AllowPrivateIPs = true
92		defer func() { AllowPrivateIPs = prev }()
93	
94		rawKey := []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
95		cases := []struct {
96			name   string
97			secret string
98			key    []byte
99		}{
100			{name: "plain secret", secret: "plain-secret-value", key: []byte("plain-secret-value")},
101			{name: "whsec_ secret", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(rawKey), key: rawKey},
102		}
103	
104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string
107				var gotBody []byte
108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
113					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
114				}))
115				defer server.Close()
116	
117				err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
118					URL:           server.URL,
119					ActivityType:  "memos.memo.created",
120					Creator:       "users/1",
121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,
122				})
123				require.NoError(t, err)
124	
125				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotID, "msg_"), "webhook-id should be prefixed with msg_")
126				require.NotEmpty(t, gotTimestamp)
127				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotSignature, "v1,"), "signature should carry the v1 version tag")
128	
129				// Recompute the signature the way a receiver would and confirm it matches.
130				mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, tc.key)
131				mac.Write([]byte(gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "."))
132				mac.Write(gotBody)
133				want := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
134				require.Equal(t, "v1,"+want, gotSignature)
135			})
136		}
137	}

Here is the complete report of my findings.

---

## 1. Webhook / Outbound HTTP Notification Delivery

### Core Webhook Dispatch Engine

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**

This is the central webhook delivery module. Key components:

- **`Post` function (line 120)** -- The synchronous webhook delivery function. Marshals a `WebhookRequestPayload` to JSON, sends an HTTP POST to the configured URL using `safeClient`, and reads/validates the response. It supports optional HMAC-SHA256 signing (Standard Webhooks protocol) via `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers (lines 133-149).

- **`PostAsync` function (line 184)** -- The asynchronous webhook delivery function. Enqueues the payload into a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128). Four background goroutines (started in `init()`, line 42-55) drain the queue and call `Post()`.

- **`safeClient` (line 32)** -- A shared `http.Client` with a 30-second timeout and a custom `Transport` that uses `safeDialContext` for SSRF protection (see section 2).

- **`WebhookRequestPayload` struct (line 79)** -- Contains `URL`, `ActivityType`, `Creator`, `Memo`, and `SigningSecret`.

- **`resolveSigningKey` (line 97)** and **`GenerateSigningSecret` (line 111)** -- Handle Standard Webhooks `whsec_<base64>` signing secret format.

### Webhook Dispatch Trigger Points (Memo Events)

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`**

- **`DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` (line 15)** -- Dispatches `memos.memo.created` event.
- **`DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (line 20)** -- Dispatches `memos.memo.updated` event.
- **`DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (line 25)** -- Dispatches `memos.memo.deleted` event.
- **`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (line 30)** -- Dispatches `memos.memo.comment.created` event to the parent memo owner's webhooks.
- **`dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (line 48)** -- Internal helper that resolves the memo creator, fetches their webhooks from the store, and calls `webhook.PostAsync()` for each (line 71).
- **`convertMemoToWebhookPayload` (line 76)** -- Converts a memo protobuf to a `WebhookRequestPayload`.

### Call Sites Where Webhooks Are Triggered

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`**
- Line 157: `s.DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage)` -- called after a memo is created.
- Line 562: `s.DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage)` -- called before a memo is deleted.

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go`**
- Line 67: `s.DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook(ctx, memoMessage)` -- called in `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` after a memo is updated.

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`**
- Line 119: `s.DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook(ctx, memoComment, relatedMemo.CreatorID)` -- called after a comment is created on a memo.

### Webhook CRUD API

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`**

- **`ListUserWebhooks` (line 20)** -- Lists all webhooks for a user.
- **`CreateUserWebhook` (line 53)** -- Creates a new webhook. Validates the URL via `webhook.ValidateURL()` (line 74). Auto-generates a signing secret if none provided (line 82).
- **`UpdateUserWebhook` (line 106)** -- Updates a webhook. Validates URL on change (lines 161, 182).
- **`DeleteUserWebhook` (line 205)** -- Deletes a webhook.
- **`GetUserWebhookSigningSecret` (line 253)** -- Reveals the signing secret (owner/admin only).

### Webhook Data Store

**`/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go`**

- **`GetUserWebhooks` (line 312)** -- Retrieves webhooks from user settings.
- **`AddUserWebhook` (line 329)** -- Persists a new webhook.
- **`RemoveUserWebhook` (line 366)** -- Removes a webhook by ID.
- **`UpdateUserWebhook` (line 393)** -- Updates a webhook in user settings.

### Other Outbound HTTP: Link Metadata Fetching

**`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go`**

- **`GetHTMLMeta` (line 136)** -- Fetches a URL and extracts HTML meta tags (title, description, og:image) for link previews. Called via `fetchHTMLMeta` from the memo service.
- Uses its own `httpClient` (line 28-48) with SSRF protection (see section 2).

**`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go`**

- **`GetLinkMetadata` (line 14)** -- API endpoint for fetching link metadata.
- **`BatchGetLinkMetadata` (line 19)** -- Batch API endpoint (max 10 URLs, defined in `memo_service.go` line 26).

**`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/image.go`**

- **`GetImage` (line 16)** -- Fetches an image from a URL. **NOTE**: This function uses the default `http.Get()` (line 21) with **NO SSRF protection** -- it does not use `validateURL` or the `secureDialContext`. However, it does not appear to be called from any server-side code currently (no call sites found in `server/` directory).

---

## 2. SSRF Protection

There are **two independent SSRF protection implementations** in this codebase:

### A. Webhook SSRF Protection (`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/`)

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go`**

- **`reservedCIDRs` (line 14)** -- A list of blocked CIDR ranges:
  - `127.0.0.0/8` (IPv4 loopback)
  - `10.0.0.0/8` (RFC-1918 class A)
  - `172.16.0.0/12` (RFC-1918 class B)
  - `192.168.0.0/16` (RFC-1918 class C)
  - `169.254.0.0/16` (link-local / cloud IMDS)
  - `::1/128` (IPv6 loopback)
  - `fc00::/7` (IPv6 unique local)
  - `fe80::/10` (IPv6 link-local)

- **`reservedNetworks` (line 26)** -- Parsed `*net.IPNet` form, built at startup in `init()` (line 28).

- **`AllowPrivateIPs` (line 41)** -- Global toggle to disable SSRF protection for self-hosted deployments targeting local network services. Currently only set to `true` in test code.

- **`isReservedIP` (line 44)** -- Checks if an IP falls within any reserved/private range. Returns `false` (allows all) when `AllowPrivateIPs` is `true`.

- **`ValidateURL` (line 62)** -- Input validation at webhook creation/update time. Checks: (1) valid absolute URL, (2) http/https scheme only, (3) DNS resolution does not yield reserved IPs. Returns gRPC `InvalidArgument` errors.

- **`ValidateSigningSecret` (line 90)** -- Validates that the signing secret contains only printable ASCII and valid base64 if using `whsec_` prefix.

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**

- **`safeDialContext` (line 59)** -- Runtime dial-time SSRF guard. Resolves the hostname, checks each resolved IP against `isReservedIP`, and refuses to connect if any IP is reserved. This guards against DNS rebinding attacks (where a hostname resolves to a safe IP during validation but to a private IP during the actual connection).

- **`safeClient` (line 32)** -- HTTP client configured with the safe transport using `safeDialContext`.

Both layers (registration-time validation via `ValidateURL` and runtime dial-time protection via `safeDialContext`) are applied to webhook delivery.

### B. Link Preview / HTTP Getter SSRF Protection (`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/`)

**`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go`**

- **`ErrInternalIP` (line 18)** -- Sentinel error for internal IP blocking.

- **`isInternalIP` (line 104)** -- Uses Go standard library methods: `ip.IsLoopback()`, `ip.IsPrivate()`, `ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast()`, `ip.IsUnspecified()`.

- **`validateURL` (line 108)** -- Input validation: checks scheme is http/https, hostname is non-empty, and IP literals are not internal.

- **`resolveAllowedIPs` (line 73)** -- Resolves a hostname and rejects if any resolved IP is internal.

- **`secureDialContext` (line 51)** -- Runtime dial-time guard: resolves the hostname via `resolveAllowedIPs`, then dials only the resolved (verified safe) IPs.

- **`newHTTPClient` (line 31)** -- Creates the HTTP client with:
  - `transport.Proxy = nil` (line 33) -- Disables proxy to prevent proxy-based SSRF bypasses.
  - `transport.DialContext = secureDialContext` (line 34) -- Uses the secure dialer.
  - `CheckRedirect` (line 39) -- Validates each redirect target URL via `validateURL` to prevent redirect-based SSRF.
  - 5-second timeout (line 38).
  - Max 10 redirects (line 43).

### Test Coverage for SSRF

**`/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook_test.go`**
- Lines 89-92, 141-143: Tests explicitly toggle `AllowPrivateIPs` to `true` when using `httptest.NewServer` (which listens on 127.0.0.1).

**`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/html_meta_test.go`**
- **`TestGetHTMLMetaForInternal` (line 126)** -- Tests that `192.168.0.1` and `localhost` are blocked with `ErrInternalIP`.
- **`TestSecureDialContextRejectsResolvedInternalIP` (line 142)** -- Tests that DNS resolution to `127.0.0.1` is blocked before dial.
- **`TestSecureDialContextDialsResolvedIP` (line 162)** -- Tests that a public IP is allowed and the resolved IP (not the hostname) is dialed.

### Notable Gap

**`/bench/repo/internal/httpgetter/image.go`, `GetImage` function (line 16)** -- Uses bare `http.Get()` with **no SSRF protection**. However, this function has no call sites in the server code, so it is not currently exploitable through the application.
